payload.description: Use Managed Disks for VM disks

learnMoreLink.name: Migrate your Azure unmanaged disks by Sep 30, 2025

payload.longDescription: Azure is retiring unmanaged disks on September 30, 2025. Users should plan the migration to avoid disruptions and maintain service reliability.

items.title: Use Managed Disks for VM disks

payload.description: Backup VMs with Azure Backup service

learnMoreLink.name: What is the Azure Backup service?

payload.longDescription: Enable backups for your virtual machines with Azure Backup to secure and quickly recover your data. This service offers simple, secure, and cost-effective solutions for backing up and recovering data from the Microsoft Azure cloud.

items.title: Backup VMs with Azure Backup service

payload.description: Run production workloads on two or more VMs using VMSS Flex

learnMoreLink.name: What has changed with Flexible orchestration mode

payload.longDescription: Production VM workloads should be deployed on multiple VMs and grouped in a VMSS Flex instance to intelligently distribute across the platform, minimizing the impact of platform faults and updates.

items.title: Run production workloads on two or more VMs using VMSS Flex

payload.description: Deploy VMs across Availability Zones

learnMoreLink.name: Create virtual machines in an availability zone using the Azure portal

payload.longDescription: Azure Availability Zones, within each Azure region, are tolerant to local failures, protecting applications and data against unlikely Datacenter failures by being physically separate.

items.title: Deploy VMs across Availability Zones

payload.description: Enable Scheduled Events for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs

learnMoreLink.name: Monitor scheduled events for your Azure VMs

payload.longDescription: If your workload is Maintenance sensitive, enable Scheduled Events. This Azure Metadata Service lets your app prepare for virtual machine maintenance by providing information on upcoming events like reboots, reducing disruptions.

items.title: Enable Scheduled Events for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs

payload.description: Reserve Compute Capacity for critical workloads

learnMoreLink.name: On-demand Capacity Reservation

payload.longDescription: Azure Capacity Reservations ensure high availability for virtual machines by reserving compute capacity in advance within a specific region or availability zone. This guarantees that VMs will have the necessary resources during peak demand or maintenance events, enhancing reliability and uptime.

items.title: Reserve Compute Capacity for critical workloads

payload.description: Don't use A or B-Series VMs for production needing constant full CPU performance

learnMoreLink.name: B-series burstable virtual machine sizes

payload.longDescription: A-series VMs are tailored for entry-level workloads like development and testing, including use cases such as development and test servers, low traffic web servers, and small to medium databases.
payload.potentialBenefits: Ensures full CPU usage for heavy tasks

items.title: Don't use A or B-Series VMs for production needing constant full CPU performance

payload.description: IP Forwarding should only be enabled for Network Virtual Appliances

learnMoreLink.name: Enable or disable IP forwarding

payload.longDescription: IP forwarding allows a virtual machine network interface to receive and send network traffic not destined for or originating from its assigned IP addresses.

items.title: IP Forwarding should only be enabled for Network Virtual Appliances

payload.description: Host database data on a data disk

learnMoreLink.name: Introduction to Azure managed disks - Data disks

payload.longDescription: A data disk is a managed disk attached to a virtual machine for storing database or other essential data. These disks are SCSI drives labeled as per choice.

items.title: Host database data on a data disk

payload.description: Use maintenance configurations for the Dedicated and/or Isolated VM SKUs

learnMoreLink.name: Use maintenance configurations to control and manage the VM updates

payload.longDescription: The maintenance configuration settings let users schedule and manage updates, making sure the updates or interruptions on the VM are performed within a planned timeframe.

items.title: Use maintenance configurations for the Dedicated and/or Isolated VM SKUs

payload.description: Reserve Compute Capacity in Disaster Recovery Regions

learnMoreLink.name: On-demand Capacity Reservation

payload.longDescription: On-Demand Capacity Reservations ensure recovery of virtual machines in the event of a natural disaster by reserving compute capacity in advance within a specific region or zone. This guarantees that VMs have the necessary resources during disaster recovery failover events thus reducing downtime.
payload.potentialBenefits: Guaranteed capacity in disaster recovery regions

items.title: Reserve Compute Capacity in Disaster Recovery Regions

payload.description: Update the Azure Linux VM Agent

learnMoreLink.name: How to update the Azure Linux Agent on a VM

payload.longDescription: If you've installed the Azure Linux Agent or are using an endorsed distribution image, ensure your agent version is up-to-date. Some Linux distributions may disable auto-update or use older agent versions.

items.title: Update the Azure Linux VM Agent

payload.description: Network access to the VM disk should be set to Disable public access and enable private access

learnMoreLink.name: Restrict import/export access for managed disks using Azure Private Link

payload.longDescription: Recommended changing to "Disable public access and enable private access" and creating a Private Endpoint to improve security by restricting direct public access and ensuring connections are made privately, enhancing data protection and minimizing potential external threats.

items.title: Network access to the VM disk should be set to Disable public access and enable private access

payload.description: When AccelNet is enabled, you must manually update the GuestOS NIC driver

learnMoreLink.name: Accelerated Networking (AccelNet) overview

payload.longDescription: When Accelerated Networking is enabled, the default Azure VNet interface in GuestOS is swapped for a Mellanox, and its driver comes from a 3rd party. Marketplace images have the latest Mellanox drivers, but post-deployment, updating the driver is the user's responsibility.

items.title: When AccelNet is enabled, you must manually update the GuestOS NIC driver

payload.description: Use Azure Boost VMs for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs

learnMoreLink.name: Microsoft Azure Boost

payload.longDescription: If the workload is Maintenance sensitive, consider Azure Boost compatible VMs. Azure Boost is designed to lessen the impact on customers when Azure maintenance activities occur on the host.

items.title: Use Azure Boost VMs for Maintenance sensitive workload VMs

payload.description: Migrate VMs using availability sets to VMSS Flex

learnMoreLink.name: Migrate deployments and resources to Virtual Machine Scale Sets in Flexible orchestration

payload.longDescription: While availability sets are not scheduled for immediate deprecation, they are planned to be deprecated in the future. Migrate workloads from VMs to VMSS Flex for deployment across zones or within the same zone across different fault domains (FDs) for better reliability.

items.title: Migrate VMs using availability sets to VMSS Flex

payload.description: Enable VM Insights

learnMoreLink.name: Overview of VM insights

payload.longDescription: VM Insights monitors VM and scale set performance, health, running processes, and dependencies. It enhances the predictability of application performance and availability by pinpointing performance bottlenecks and network issues, and it clarifies if problems are related to other dependencies.

items.title: Enable VM Insights

payload.description: Replicate VMs using Azure Site Recovery

learnMoreLink.name: Resiliency checklist for Virtual Machines

payload.longDescription: Replicating Azure VMs via Site Recovery entails continuous, asynchronous disk replication to a target region. Recovery points are generated every few minutes, ensuring a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in minutes.

items.title: Replicate VMs using Azure Site Recovery

payload.description: Mission Critical Workloads should consider using Premium or Ultra Disks

learnMoreLink.name: Disk type comparison and decision tree

payload.longDescription: Compared to Standard HDD and SSD, Premium SSD, SSD v2, and Ultra Disks offer improved performance, configurability, and higher single-instance VM uptime SLAs. The lowest SLA of all disks on a VM applies, so it is best to use Premium or Ultra Disks for the highest uptime SLA.
payload.potentialBenefits: Enhanced performance, cost efficiency, and uptime SLA

items.title: Mission Critical Workloads should consider using Premium or Ultra Disks

payload.description: Enable Accelerated Networking (AccelNet)

learnMoreLink.name: Accelerated Networking (AccelNet) overview

payload.longDescription: Accelerated networking enables SR-IOV to a VM, greatly improving its networking performance by bypassing the host from the data path, which reduces latency, jitter, and CPU utilization for demanding network workloads on supported VM types.
payload.potentialBenefits: Reduces latency, jitter and CPU use

items.title: Enable Accelerated Networking (AccelNet)
